question:
A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician for the evaluation of fatigue for the past 6 months. During this period, she has had a 5-kg (11-lbs) weight loss. She states that she has no friends. When she is not in school, she spends most of her time in bed. She has no history of serious illness. Her mother has major depressive disorder. She appears pale and thin. She is at 25th percentile for height, 10th percentile for weight, and 20th percentile for BMI; her BMI is 19.0. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 65/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows dry skin, brittle nails, and calluses on the knuckles. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12.3 g/dL
Serum
Na+ 133 mEq/L
Cl- 90 mEq/L
K+ 3.2 mEq/L
HCO3- 30 mEq/L
Ca+2 7.8 mg/dL
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fatigue for the past 6 months" -> "5-kg weight loss" -> "Social withdrawal and isolation" -> "Spends most of her time in bed" -> "No serious illness history" -> "Mother has major depressive disorder" -> "Pale and thin appearance" -> "Dry skin, brittle nails, calluses on knuckles" -> "Low BMI (19.0)" -> "Laboratory findings: low hemoglobin (12.3 g/dL), low serum Ca+2 (7.8 mg/dL), low K+ (3.2 mEq/L)" -> "Possible diagnosis of anorexia nervosa" -> 80%
analysis: The most likely diagnosis for this 17-year-old girl with fatigue, weight loss, social withdrawal, and physical signs of malnutrition is anorexia nervosa. The low BMI, electrolyte abnormalities, and characteristic behaviors support this diagnosis.
